items.title: 67251_Chuck Green oral history interview
items.q: And one of our dancers in this show -- he's a tap dancer known as Sad Man Sims, you see.

ctx.x: Now, the audience is very happy, see. It takes right away. And then the critics started coming in there. I think there was a few critics' secretaries was there. Lot of stars was in the audience, you know, like Nipsy Russell. He's from my home state, you see. And there they call the dancing chauffeur up there now.

And one of our dancers in this show -- he's a tap dancer known as Sad Man Sims, you see. And he had one of our partner's names which was Howards. So anyhow, he did an on the town dance, Raymond Kaleland. Now the next one comes out, you see (unintelligible) see, and he does an on the town dance, you see. And that's what it was reminiscing with Chuck Green was all about on the town, you see. And that's the only kind of out of town trade and so forth and so on, see, and they was trying to keep public relations on…

And it become what they called -- the critics finally wrote about it. They said it was a sleeper hit, you know. And this lady, Anna Kisselegoff -- I should bring you the copy of the writeup. I should have had it to you before, you know. But that's what it all consisted of, you know. And some film company was -- had some kind of apprentice, you know, a fellow named Russell Schwartz.
